title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government has issued a formal response to the 2020 Committee report on Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards, outlining its stance on how AI should be governed. It emphasizes commitments to transparency, accountability, and safety in AI deployment, and outlines steps to strengthen public trust and regulatory oversight.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual has set out how it will oversee and manage the use of artificial intelligence in qualifications, aiming to keep exams fair, secure and reliable. The policy will give clear rules, monitoring procedures and guidance to exam boards and providers so that AI tools help, rather than harm, the integrity of assessment.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report evaluates how copyrighted materials are used when training and developing AI systems, and analyzes the legal and ethical implications of that practice. It offers recommendations for balancing the interests of creators, users, and AI developers to promote responsible innovation while respecting copyright law.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has issued a response to the House of Lords AI committee’s report, “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency,” outlining its plans to boost innovation while safeguarding public interests. It highlights commitments to strengthen data and safety standards, increase investment in AI research, and establish clear regulatory frameworks to keep the UK competitive and protect society.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: The document outlines the scope, purpose, and responsibilities of a committee that will review how artificial intelligence relates to public standards. It also includes FAQs that clarify the committee’s approach and expected outcomes.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence, outlining its perspective on how AI should be regulated. The submission discusses current challenges in AI governance and offers recommendations for stronger oversight and policy development.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The policy explains how artificial intelligence will influence the rules for medical products, focusing on safety, effectiveness and clear oversight. It follows the AI White Paper principles, calling for responsible design, thorough testing, and continuous monitoring of AI-enabled medical devices.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make our country the most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential defense organization in AI, relative to its size. It focuses on building advanced AI capabilities, ensuring ethical use, and partnering with industry and allies to maintain a technological edge.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport AI Action Plan explains how the Department for Transport will partner with industry to use artificial intelligence to improve transport services and create new opportunities. It also outlines the steps the DfT will take to identify, assess and manage the risks associated with deploying AI in the transport sector.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: This report reviews how copyrighted material has been used to train AI systems, focusing on compliance with the Data (Use and Access) Act. It highlights progress made, challenges faced, and recommends steps to balance innovation with copyright protection.
